entries.headline: Before /dev:run-slice: push slice 039's three unpushed commits — Charts cfae346, ChartsDeploy 69ecb9f, RegistryDeploy e53c36b
body: Slice 039 was delivered ad hoc on 2026-10-03 and its commits in three repos were still ahead of origin when 038 was planned: Charts cfae346 (README: ChartsDeploy takes homelab-shared from charts.home) in /work/Charts, and the tarball reverts ChartsDeploy 69ecb9f and RegistryDeploy e53c36b in their /work/scratch clones. 038's P4 pushes Charts' main to publish the library (ruling D3), and P5 bumps both deploy repos in those clones, which the test phase then pushes. Left unpushed, 039's commits would go out inside 038's pushes, which no ruling of 038's authorizes, and P5's bump would not be the clone's only commit ahead.
entries.consequence: The run loop does not start while this is open; run anyway, 038's Charts publish and rollout pushes would carry slice 039's commits to origin with them.
entries.proposal: do it — push the three from their current clones (the 039 session's own pushes), then strike this entry.
entries.author: plan-writer, planning, r2, plan.md Ordering constraints and P5

strike.reason: already pushed: Charts cfae346, ChartsDeploy 69ecb9f and RegistryDeploy e53c36b are all on origin/main (verified 2026-10-03)

entries.headline: AnsibleSpecs argo-cd/decisions.md D17 still tells the charts deploy repo to vendor the library, which slice 039 reverted
body: D17 (argo-cd/decisions.md:188-189): 'Trap for when Charts itself migrates: its chart must not consume the library it serves — vendor the helper there or keep it helper-free.' Slice 039 (2026-10-03) reverted the vendoring in ChartsDeploy and RegistryDeploy, and argo-cd/design.md:133-141 now says no deploy repo commits the library tarball and a rebuilt cluster brings charts.home back by hand (Ansible docs/runbooks/cluster-bootstrap.md). design.md moved; the decision register did not.
entries.consequence: A reader of D17 is told to vendor the library into ChartsDeploy — the shape slice 039 deliberately removed — with nothing in the register pointing at the by-hand bootstrap.
entries.proposal: fix now — one '> **Amended 2026-10-03 (slice 039)**' note under D17 in the register's own style, pointing at design.md and the cluster-bootstrap runbook.
entries.author: plan-writer, planning, r2, argo-cd/decisions.md D17 against design.md

entries.headline: Settle V09 after the operator's next KubeCoder/Promote-PRD run, which moves …
body: V09 — kubecoder-prd, which tracks KubeCoderDeploy's `prd` branch (ArgoCDDeploy releases/values.yaml:172-174), syncs at the bump once promotion carries it to `prd`, and its PreSync hook runs.

`verification.json` marks V09 owed after: the operator's next KubeCoder/Promote-PRD run, which moves KubeCoderDeploy's `prd` branch. The run cannot take that action; settle the criterion once it has happened.
entries.consequence: V09 stays unproven until then; the test phase does not settle it.
entries.proposal: When that has happened, say so: the session settles V09 in verification.json.
entries.author: `verification.json`'s `owed_after`, seeded by the plan loop

entries.headline: ArgoCDDeploy render gate: the three role:readonly widenings are witnessed once, not held by a standing refusal check
body: P2's check_readonly_account refuses a role:readonly-subject rule and holds the kubecoder binding across every policy.*.csv key; the three reds (p, role:readonly, ...; g, role:readonly, role:admin; a policy.overlay.csv binding kubecoder to role:admin) were witnessed on scratch edits of config/prd/values.yaml, per the plan. Nothing in tests/render-chart.py renders those overlays on every run, the way check_setting_refusals does for autoSync, so a later edit that loosens policy_lines or the check keeps the gate green.
entries.consequence: A later regression of the role:readonly or overlay-key check passes the gate unnoticed; the check is right today.
entries.author: code-writer, P2, r1, ArgoCDDeploy tests/render-chart.py (63c370f)

entries.headline: ArgoCDDeploy render gate: a CSV-quoted subject ("role:readonly", "kubecoder") gets past check_readonly_account
body: policy_lines (tests/render-chart.py:1248-1253) splits each line on ',' and strips whitespace, and it does not remove CSV quotes. Argo CD reads policy lines with Go's encoding/csv (util/rbac loadPolicyLine — from memory, not checked against v3.5.1), which does. So 'p, "role:readonly", applications, sync, */*, allow' passes the new role:readonly refusal (:1279) while Argo enforces it, and 'g, "kubecoder", role:admin' gets past the binding check (:1272) in the same way. The binding-check half predates slice 038.
entries.consequence: A widening written with quoted fields renders green and reaches prd: the kubecoder token can then do more than read, and the gate does not say so.
entries.proposal: card — have policy_lines parse each line with Python's csv module, so the gate reads the subject the way Argo does; low priority, since only a deliberately quoted line gets through.
entries.author: code-reviewer, P2, r1, phases/P2/code_review_r1.md F1

entries.headline: The driver left a scratch clone at /work/scratch/FieldnotesDeploy (`Target: github:pvginkel/FieldnotesDeploy`)
body: The driver cloned (or adopted) `/work/scratch/FieldnotesDeploy` for `Target: github:pvginkel/FieldnotesDeploy`; the slice's phases for that repo are branched, merged and pushed there.

Deleting it is safe once the slice's commits are on origin — the push check before the doc phase confirms that. The close-out session removes it then and says so under this entry; nothing is asked of the operator. A clone left in place is synced by every later preflight in this environment and adopted by the next `github:` target naming that repo.
entries.consequence: none — the clone is where the run works; left behind, it takes disk space and a sync in every later preflight, until the close-out session removes it.
entries.author: the driver's target resolution
